tasks.short: Develop or test new methods or models of transportation analysis.

steps.what: Define the transportation analysis question, proposed method, evaluation measures and holdout test plan
Gather actual network, travel demand and observed traffic data; capture or resolve missing units, dates and identifiers
Implement and run the proposed analytical method in the transportation modelling tool and prepare fixed validation comparisons
outputs: candidate model and actual validation outputs

steps.what: Evaluate actual validation errors, bias and sensitivity and decide whether the method is useful for the specified transport question
inputs: candidate model and actual validation outputs
outputs: evaluated model limitations and acceptance decision

steps.what: Write and check the final method, actual tests and limitations record before internal retention
inputs: evaluated model limitations and acceptance decision
candidate model and actual validation outputs
outputs: approved method and validation record v1

steps.what: Save the approved method and validation record in the same internal project workspace
inputs: approved method and validation record v1

tasks.design: Try native imports and scenario comparison in the transportation modelling tool {OTHER}, then add a deterministic validation script in {DATA_PLATFORM} only for repeated calculations it lacks. The planner designs the method, evaluates actual holdout performance and checks the final record before saving; no model is automatically accepted or deployed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated unit conversions and validation calculations are mixed with method development.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned scripts and native scenario comparisons can rerun specified calculations.
tasks.still_hard: A good fit on historic observations may fail on a changed transport network.
tasks.human_edge: The planner chooses valid tests and interprets causal and behavioural limits.

ambition.what: Compare a candidate transport method against a fixed holdout before using it in a study.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated calculation; analytical acceptance remains human.

reach.learn: Holdout testing and transport data quality

evidence.claim: Transport modelling tools and versioned analytical scripts support repeatable scenario and validation calculations.

assumptions: Provisional shares, not measured baseline. Boundary is a candidate analytical method and test record; no live traffic control or official model adoption. OTHER is the transportation modelling application.

s2 captures network link/node IDs, geometry version, mode, time period, trips, observed counts, units and provenance from actual existing datasets; missing observations and metadata are resolved manually within retained effort. No synthetic observations substitute for missing field data.

s1 supplies the algorithm, metrics, holdout and tolerances. s3 reduces only repeated transforms and metric computation, retaining implementation and debugging. Runtime of an existing solver earns no labour saving. Method judgement in s4 stays full.
s5 includes authoring and final checking of the completed record; edits restart its check. The same-workspace save retains full human effort and earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual repeated validation effort and native tool coverage
Availability of independent observed traffic data
research_questions: Which recurring validation calculations remain manual after native configuration?

incremental.description: Maintain validation code and data mappings

approvals.approved_version: method and actual validation record v1 checked in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: novel methods need nearly all manual preparation, leaving two gross points offset by two upkeep points. High: repeatable metric and import work saves twelve gross points less upkeep, below central net10.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate transportation consequences of legislative proposals.

steps.what: Obtain the exact legislative proposal version and affected transport context and identify missing source material
outputs: versioned proposal and checked transport context

steps.what: Read proposal provisions and prepare a source-linked map of potential transport mechanisms, conditions and uncertainties
inputs: versioned proposal and checked transport context

loop.purpose: Prepare a bounded first reading of proposal provisions
loop.input: Exact proposal text and checked transport context only
loop.output: Potential transport mechanisms with provision citations and uncertainty flags
loop.check: Planner reads each linked provision and verifies conditions, scope and meaning; unsupported effects are removed
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; ambiguous provisions return to manual analysis
loop.why_not_simpler: Conditional prose and interactions between provisions need interpretation; a fixed field template cannot identify their meaning

steps.what: Evaluate actual transport consequences, alternatives and uncertainties using relevant data and expert judgement
inputs: versioned proposal and checked transport context

steps.what: Write the final transport impact assessment and check all consequential claims against the proposal and actual analysis
inputs: versioned proposal and checked transport context

steps.what: Save the approved impact assessment in the same internal document workspace

tasks.design: Keep an exact proposal snapshot in {DOCS}; test native search before using a bounded model first reading of relevant provisions. The planner checks provision meaning, performs the impact evaluation and checks the completed assessment before internal retention.
tasks.previous_blocker: Long conditional proposal text makes an initial mechanism map slow to assemble.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded text loop can propose cited mechanisms while retaining full human consequence analysis.
tasks.still_hard: Effects depend on implementation, behaviour and legal interpretation beyond text matching.
tasks.human_edge: The planner distinguishes plausible transport effects from unsupported causal claims.

ambition.what: No automatic policy recommendation or legal conclusion.

tasks.altitude: Faster first reading; policy judgement and accountability are unchanged.

evidence.claim: A bounded text model can propose source-linked summaries that require substantive human verification.

assumptions: Provisional shares. Boundary is an internal transport impact assessment of a proposal, not current-law advice or a public submission. OTHER is the transport analysis tool used for supporting scenarios.

s1 planner obtains proposal ID, jurisdiction, version/date, full text and available actual baseline network/demand evidence; missing evidence is sought manually and recorded as uncertain, never invented. s3 produces all scenario assumptions and effect judgements at full effort; existing supporting calculations are not claimed as new saving.

Native text search and structured provision headings are tried first. s2's retained 70% includes passage-by-passage meaning checks, correction and manual analysis of ambiguous clauses. No external facts or citations are generated.
s4 completes the actual assessment then checks its claims; changes require another final check. Same-workspace save retains full human effort. No distribution is assumed in the baseline.
unknowns: Actual proposal length and first-reading effort
Available baseline data and specialist interpretation needs
research_questions: Does a bounded mechanism map reduce total reading after checking every relevant provision?

already_counted.description: Substantive checking and correction of the first-reading map

incremental.description: Maintain restricted document access and evaluate drafting failures

approvals.approved_version: transport impact assessment v1 completed and checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: novel or ambiguous clauses remove all first-reading benefit and upkeep remains. High: a stable proposal allows6.5 gross points less1.5 upkeep, below central net6; effect evaluation stays full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design improved transport infrastructure including junctions, pedestrian projects, bus facilities or parking.

steps.what: Inspect actual site conditions and gather network geometry, observed use and transport design requirements
inputs: actual junction, pedestrian, bus or parking site
outputs: checked site geometry and infrastructure requirements

steps.what: Develop alternative transport layouts and resolve movement, access, safety and land constraints
inputs: checked site geometry and infrastructure requirements

steps.what: Produce layout drawings and calculate specified dimensions and quantities for the candidate designs
inputs: checked site geometry and infrastructure requirements

steps.what: Evaluate the actual layout and dimension results, correct the design and approve the completed internal concept version
inputs: checked site geometry and infrastructure requirements

steps.what: Save the approved infrastructure concept in the same internal design workspace

tasks.design: Configure reusable drawing objects and dimension schedules in the existing transport design application {OTHER}. Keep actual site capture, layout choices and final technical review human; the same-workspace save retains full effort and the design remains an internal concept.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated drawing and dimension annotation compete with actual layout design.
tasks.enabler_now: Native drawing references, reusable objects and dimension schedules can reduce repeated annotation.
tasks.still_hard: Safe movement, accessibility and competing land needs cannot be decided by a drawing template.
tasks.human_edge: The planner balances real movement needs and judges whether the design works on site.

ambition.what: Compare another feasible infrastructure layout before selecting the concept.

tasks.altitude: Less annotation, with unchanged concept-design authority.

evidence.claim: Native transport design and drafting tools can reuse objects and produce dimension schedules from explicit geometry.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover internal concept design, not construction approval, road closure orders or public issue. OTHER is the transport drafting/GIS application.

s1 captures actual site geometry/version, survey date, observed movements, constraints and applicable design dimensions from existing surveys and site work; missing measurements remain manual within full s1. s2 produces each proposed geometry and layout choice. s3 schedules only explicit geometry, with no inferred utilities, land rights or accessibility compliance.

Native reusable objects and dimensions are tested first. s3 retains all custom drafting and correction effort; no runtime benefit is credited. s4 checks the finished design before save; changes require a fresh check. Same-system save earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual repeated drafting effort and native object coverage
Required surveys and specialist design approvals
research_questions: Which dimension annotations are still manually repeated in the existing design application?

already_counted.description: Completed concept technical check and correction

incremental.description: Maintain reusable drawing objects and schedules

approvals.approved_version: infrastructure concept v1 after final technical review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual site geometry yields only one gross point offset by upkeep. High: repeated objects and schedules save seven gross points less one upkeep point, below central net6.5; site work and layout judgement remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define or update urban boundaries or roadway classifications.

steps.what: Collect the current authoritative urban boundary or road classification data and actual change evidence
outputs: checked boundary or classification change inputs

steps.what: Determine the proposed boundary or roadway classification changes against actual evidence and applicable criteria
inputs: checked boundary or classification change inputs
outputs: judged proposed boundary or classification edits

steps.what: Prepare the revised working layer and change record and check geometry validity, required fields and old/new differences
inputs: judged proposed boundary or classification edits
checked boundary or classification change inputs
outputs: final revised working layer and change record v1

steps.what: Check the complete revised layer and change record against the evidence and approve the exact internal update
inputs: final revised working layer and change record v1
checked boundary or classification change inputs
outputs: approved working layer and change record v1

steps.what: Commit the approved working layer and change record in the same internal GIS workspace
inputs: approved working layer and change record v1
outputs: committed working boundary or classification update

tasks.design: Configure versioned GIS layers, explicit field checks and change comparison in {OTHER}. The planner decides each boundary or classification change and checks the finished layer before the separate internal commit; official designation or public publication needs its own later authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes can be manually copied and checked against different geometry versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native GIS imports, version comparisons and topology checks can expose mechanical errors.
tasks.still_hard: Classification and urban boundary definitions need evidence and accountable interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The planner judges whether the real change meets the applicable criteria.

ambition.what: No new official designation rights are assumed.

tasks.altitude: Less mechanical layer checking; decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Validate a revised transport reference layer

evidence.claim: GIS software can compare explicit layer versions and validate geometry and required fields.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover working reference-data definition and update, not legal designation or public issue. OTHER is the GIS application; native configuration is tried first.

s1 planner obtains layer ID/version, feature ID, geometry/coordinate system, current classification, dated source evidence and approved classification criteria; missing metadata or evidence is manually resolved within retained time. s2 produces the proposed geometry/class and reason. No absent policy criterion is invented.

s3 reuses selected feature IDs, checks geometry and displays differences; it retains manual editing and exception handling. s4 verifies meaning against source evidence, not just topology. Same-system commit retains full human effort and earns no saving; a changed edit requires fresh approval.
If an authority's adopted layer is the target, an additional authority decision and version-bound gate must be counted before use.
unknowns: Which authority approves official classification changes
research_questions: Does native GIS version comparison preserve the required source and change history?

incremental.description: Maintain GIS validation fields and import mappings

approvals.approved_version: working boundary or classification layer and change record v1

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: inconsistent source layers allow only three gross points less one upkeep point. High: stable feature IDs enable fourteen gross points less upkeep, below central net13.5; all classification judgement remains full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The planner spends less time preparing repeatable calculations and layer checks while retaining scientific and policy judgement.
role.ambitious_version: Compare more transport design and method options against actual evidence before recommending one.
